_README:
Pet level economics. THIS FILE IS EMPTY ON PURPOSE and the app works without it.

Nothing in the game client relates feedPower to a pet level. Swept all 246 XML files: there is no petXP, no xpRequired, no FeedRate, no per-rarity level cap, and no definition for the four curve names pets.xml uses (exp_incr, dim_returns, exp_decr, linear). The endpoints of every ability are in the client and are shown in the app; everything between them, and the whole feed-to-level relationship, is server-side.

So this is the one place the app will accept numbers that did NOT come out of the game files, and it labels them as such wherever it uses them. Fill it in from a community table you trust (the RotMG subreddit's pet spreadsheet is the usual one), then re-run build.ps1.

HOW TO FILL IT IN

  source      A sentence naming where the numbers came from. The app prints this next to
              every number it derives from this file, so a reader can judge it. If this is
              blank the app treats the file as absent.

  maxLevel    Pet rarity -> the highest level that rarity can reach.
              e.g. {"Common": 30, "Uncommon": 50, "Rare": 70, "Legendary": 90, "Divine": 100}
              Note the client's pets.xml only ever says Common / Rare / Divine, while
              equipEggs.xml only ever says Common / Uncommon / Rare / Legendary. Where
              Divine sits relative to Legendary is not stated anywhere in the client.

  feedToLevel A list of [level, cumulativeFeedPower] pairs, ascending by level, where the
              second number is the TOTAL feed power spent to reach that level from level 1.
              Partial tables are fine - the app interpolates nothing and simply says a
              level is not in the table.
              e.g. [[1, 0], [2, 20], [3, 45]]

The app never guesses past what is here. A missing level says so; it does not extrapolate.
